reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports that multi-element alloy barriers increase failure temperature and activation energy for diffusion in Cu/Si systems, but it does not address Cr–Zr interdiffusion, the specific HEA composition (TiTaCrZrAl), ultra-thin (~10 nm) layer feasibility, or effects on adhesion and corrosion in the proposed environment. Key premises about the specific material system and performance are unsupported.
premises: Multi-element alloy barriers increase failure temperature against interdiffusion
Activation energy for diffusion increases with number of elements in the alloy
Lattice distortion and high cohesive energy suppress vacancy formation and atomic mobility
An ultra-thin (~10 nm) HEA interlayer can effectively block Cr–Zr interdiffusion
The HEA interlayer will maintain adhesion and corrosion resistance under operational and accident conditions
